newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope opens way for proclamation of Polish saints.
newsitem.headline: Pope opens way for proclamation of Polish saints.

text.p: Pope John Paul has attributed miracles to two Polish candidates for sainthood, opening the way for them to be canonised when he travels to Poland next month, the Vatican said in a statement on Tuesday.

Edith Stein, a victim of the Nazi holocaust, and 14th century Queen Edvige of Poland have both already been beatified by the Roman Catholic Church for performing one miracle. Beatification is the first step on the road to sainthood.
A second miracle means both can now be proclaimed saints when the Polish Pontiff visits his homeland for an 11-day trip starting on May 31. The Vatican gave no details of the miracles.
Sister Theresa Blessed of the Cross, Stein's religious title, died in Auschwitz in 1942 after leaving the Jewish faith to become a nun. Her beatification was criticised by Jewish groups.
Queen Edvige of Poland died in 1399 aged just 22 and is one of the Polish Catholic church's most respected figures.
